before.exam_tip_html: For questions about reasons for crime, examiners want to see that you understand the complexity of the issue. Do not simply list reasons — explain how religious believers would respond to each reason with specific teachings. For the 12-mark evaluation, you might consider whether criminals deserve punishment or compassion, using religious evidence to support both sides.

For questions about forgiveness, examiners want to see that you understand the tension between forgiveness and justice. Do not assume they are opposites — religious teaching shows they can coexist. Use specific real-world examples (Gee Walker, Desmond Tutu, the Amish community) to support your arguments. For the 12-mark evaluation, consider whether forgiveness is always possible, or whether some crimes are too severe to forgive.

For questions on Zakah, explain both the spiritual purpose (purification of wealth, obedience to God) and the social purpose (reducing poverty, strengthening the ummah). For Hajj questions, be specific about the rituals and their significance — examiners reward students who can explain why each ritual is performed, not just what happens. Always link rituals back to Ibrahim. In “Explain Similarities & Differences” questions, Zakah vs Khums is an excellent comparison point.
